items.title: Poland: Lifeline for Ukrainian refugees confronts donor fatigue and online abuse as anti-Ukrainian sentiment grows
items.description: A Ukrainian woman who fled the war in her country built a lifeline for refugees in Poland. Now her organization faces donor fatigue, funding cuts and rising hostility as support for Ukrainians in Poland wanes.

items.title: How the Trump administration wages its diplomatic offensive against abortion rights
items.description: Since the abrupt halt of USAID, bilateral agreements driven by American interests have replaced humanitarian aid. One of the key provisions is the refusal to fund the promotion or practice of abortion, especially in Africa.

items.title: Eritrea and Ethiopia accuse each other of provoking war as Tigray rebels retreat
items.description: Ethiopia and Eritrea on Friday accused each other of starting a "war of agresson" days after the two countries severed diplomatic ties. Ethiopian officals estimate that up to 8,000 Eritrean soldiers are present in Tigray supporting rebels who last month launched attacks against federal forces.

items.title: Is Trump signalling a return to war with Iran after the midterms?
items.description: US media reports suggest he may be weighing strikes before the vote, but the president has ruled that out.

items.title: South Korea recalls Ukraine envoy over prisoner-of-war row
items.description: It is the latest in a diplomatic spat after Kyiv disclosed that two North Korean prisoners were transferred to Seoul.

items.title: Darfur: Healthcare needs outstrip resources as Security Council extends Sudan sanctions
items.description: More than 700,000 displaced people in Tawila, in Sudan’s war-ravaged Darfur region, face severe shortages of healthcare, food, water and protection, the UN World Health Organization (WHO) warned on Thursday as it called for an urgent increase in resources.

items.title: Russian strikes on Ukraine's public buses leave 30 dead as blackouts worsen in Kyiv
items.description: Russia and Ukraine are locked in a long-range aerial war while their armies remain largely deadlocked on the front line, more than 4 1/2 years since Moscow's full-scale invasion.

items.title: Dozens Killed In Russian Strike On Passenger Buses In Kramatorsk
items.description: Dozens of people were killed in a Russian strike on the Ukrainian city of Kramatorsk on October 8, according to local authorities, a day after another deadly barrage killed at least 25 people across Ukraine.

items.title: EU Lifts Belarus-Related Sanctions on Russian Billionaire Gutseriev – RFE/RL

items.title: In Ukraine, holding on to childhood in a time of war
items.description: As war in Ukraine continues into its fifth year, some children have only known war. The Monitor revisits three young families striving to live full lives amid Russia’s military invasion.
